units.translation: And graciously send these good things from him to your husband Darius
There he sends these men
Send libations to the chambers beneath the earth
Send up from below the soul to the light
Earth and you other lords of the underworld – send up from below the one such as Persia has never yet covered
I will send a tearful cry
I will send you with mournful laments
He sends the Erinys who brings later punishment upon transgressors
Zeus, the god of hospitality, sends the sons of Atreus against Alexander
The warlike bird sends the twin commanders of the youth of Hellas to the land of Teucer
They send a great beard of flame
For he knows whom someone sent
He sends a heavy dust to his friends
And the hero those who sent him
Those who sent them forward brought them back again
To those who send these things
He sent a lock of hair
You would be able to send signs that are persuasive to mortals
Send help to the children
From where did she send libations?
She sent these libations
And then she sends these funeral libations
And the children of Hephaestus send him
And he sent me back from the house of Loxias, terrible to behold with my eyes
I commanded to send punishments for my father
Both to remain and to send these things, and he is in helpless distress
And my father will send help from the tomb
And I sent this man as a suppliant at your hearth
But to send what is profitable for the victory of the city
And I will send the light of torches
Send the insolent swarm, born of Egypt, to the sea
A stormless ship sent me with friendly breezes
But may the earth receive well what he sent well
And graciously send our father here
Everyone who passed by sent a charming arrow from his eyes upon the beautiful adornments of the maidens
He sends the Sphinx, the dog that presides over evil days
No day yet sent Actaeon home empty of prey, rich in toil
But to the dead, not to the living, was the wretched favor sent
And indeed he had been sent, holding no boast in his hands
I was sending
I sent
I will send
I was being sent
he has been sent
I was sent
Who will stand with such a man as this?
short
But to send these grievous things is helpless for me
written: he has been sent
breath, ray, drop

The genitive πέμφιγος [of πέμφιξ] has the middle syllable long. Galen discussed this word learnedly and copiously in vol. 5 p. 454 of the Basel edition (vol. 9 p. 385 of the Chartier edition), citing examples of its three meanings: πνοή [breath], flatus; ἀκτίς [ray], solar ray; pavis, gutta [drop].
He also noted the first and second meanings
